verdicts.claim: Training dummy: each new pairing needs at least 3 captures and a mash-on-the-dummy scene per fighter in both modes.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule is wired into the flash set: sources.json lists mashdummy, blastdummy and signaturedummy for both fighters and the dummy pairings with 7 and 6 seeds; the dummy (REFERENCE) is in the roster at HEAD and in the public pin. But no recorded pixel pass covers them (release-pass.json is for d3f1ca0e, 2026-10-15, with 0 dummy rows), the CI event count has not run since 2026-11-06, and the selftest only demands 1 seed per pairing, not 3. Not checked: any unrecorded pixel run of the dummy clips.
proof: tools/flash/sources.json pairings: PROTAGONIST v REFERENCE 7 seeds, RIVAL v REFERENCE 6 seeds
tools/flash/release-pass.json: commit d3f1ca0e, recorded 2026-10-15, no dummy rows
verdicts.fix: Make tools/flash/selftest.js require at least 3 seeds for a pairing new in a release, and record a pixel pass that includes the dummy rows before any build with full effects ships.

verdicts.claim: Ten biome signature names and TIDE CLEAVE/LANE SWEEP are clear; fire and flood variants join the flash set when built.
verdicts.what_is_true: The name clearances are Legal naming, not flash. The ten names are proposed rows in sigvariants.json, not built (only HORIZON CLEAVE, BOULEVARD RAZE, FIELD SCAR, FIRESTORM, GLASS TRENCH, RIDGE BORE are asBuilt), so the flash condition has not triggered yet. Nothing in tools/flash ties a newly built variant to the flash set, so the condition depends on someone remembering it.
proof: data/combat/sigvariants.json: GRASSLAND BLAZE, MIRE BOIL, SHORE SCOUR, CRUST SEAR etc. carry no asBuilt flag
verdicts.fix: Add a flash selftest that fails when an asBuilt fire or flood variant has no flash scene; carry the naming half in Legal's naming record, not the flash theme.

verdicts.claim: Hard flash row energy.flash: no more than three full flashes in any 60 ticks, at least 20 ticks apart, for a mashed RB + X.
verdicts.what_is_true: The row is built and the sim enforces it from data (flashEveryTicks 20, so at most 3 eligible landings in a 60-tick window); three QA runs record PASS (most in 60 ticks 3, shortest gap 20). The record is stale: plan :143 still says Paper and the status says PENDING until the cue exists, but the cue exists. It counts sim events, not pixels; the renderer also asks the register and draws no energy full flash at all under Reduce flashing, which is locked on in /play/.
proof: docs/qa/c2-second-round-f9469f8a.md:359 PASS energy.flash, most in 60 ticks 3, shortest gap 20
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed); the stale PENDING and Paper labels invite re-work on a row that already passes.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record to Built and PASS, and keep describing it as an event-rate check, not a photosensitivity reading.

verdicts.claim: GB-003: the split-screen camera jolts when a player is knocked away.
verdicts.what_is_true: Orb's report is real, and Camera answered it the same day: d7323551 (2026-10-02, two hours after GB-003 was logged) added a jolt pass and a per-tick jolt scan to split_sweep, whose doc records 4,636 jolts cut to 1,572 and later 1,546 still counted. So known-bugs.md:179's 'no metric exists' is stale. A camera jolt is a feel and comfort bug, not a seizure or legal risk.
proof: git log: 965cdbc2 2026-10-02 02:19 adds GB-003; d7323551 2026-10-02 04:22 Camera split-screen jolt pass
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Carried as a flash-theme item with 'no metric', it can make QA build a camera metric that Camera's sweep already has.
verdicts.fix: Move to Camera's queue; QA re-reads it against split_sweep's jolt scan and closes or re-opens it with a number.

verdicts.claim: In spectating and replays the viewer's own setting applies. Above 1x playback every swing is shown as a cut, and seeking snaps the view, never animating through a skipped swing.
verdicts.what_is_true: Partly built, despite the record: split_rig.gd:5517 shows swings as cuts when playback is above 1x, world_turning is 'cut', or 'auto' with Reduced motion, and a replay seek re-seats the view (:714). Nothing calls set_playback, NetSpectator is used only by the loopback harness, and the world swing is not in the public pin, so no viewer can reach this today. The spectator's catch-up (up to 3 ticks a frame) would need to pass its rate to set_playback when a view is built. Motion comfort, not seizure risk.
proof: render/camera/split_rig.gd:5517 return playback > 1.0 or world_turning == "cut" or (world_turning == "auto" and reduced_motion)
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed); the stale 'not built' status could prompt duplicate work.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record (the hook exists); when a spectator or replay view is built, have it call set_playback with its real rate, including catch-up, and add a test.

verdicts.claim: Open asks: seed Reduced motion from the platform's preference, and ask Legal whether a motion line with its own buttons may sit beside the flash notice on first run.
verdicts.what_is_true: Both asks are real and open: no code in ui, render, tools, sim or net reads prefers-reduced-motion, and the review log has no answer on a motion line. Seeding the setting is an accessibility feature, and where a motion line sits beside the notice is a UI layout choice that no cited law or standard governs. Neither is a release-safety finding.
proof: git grep prefers-reduced-motion over ui render tools sim net: 0 files
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A Legal ask in the safety queue for a UI layout question, and a feature request that looks like a safety gap.
verdicts.fix: Move both to the Accessibility and UI backlog as a feature ticket (seed reduced_motion from the browser's preference on web); retire the Legal question or make it the EP's UI call.

verdicts.claim: Blast amplification for power-up craters is GO on eight conditions.
verdicts.what_is_true: The eight conditions exist (agency-pass-screen.md:82-90, a file the log row does not name) and VFX built and tested them (POWERUP_OFF, blast_powerup_enabled, effects_check _blast). Most are staging distance from a well-known franchise's transformation (scream, crouch, aura, hair change, levitating rocks). Condition 3's 'no gold, white or red flash' is the one light rule, and the flash register already refuses red (flash_registry.gd:20). So this is an originality ruling, not a flash condition.
proof: docs/legal/agency-pass-screen.md:85 condition 3: no lightning, flame aura, hair change, gold, white or red flash
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It reads as an open flash condition 'until the first transformation cinematic' and keeps a flash re-screen on the list for what is really an originality check.
verdicts.fix: Move to Legal's originality record and correct the log row to name agency-pass-screen.md; the flash side is already covered by the register.

verdicts.claim: The dynamic sky passes: slow, 0.05 a band a second, no pulse. Town glow fades in over 1 s or more, and the body's white on a hit is held lower for comfort.
verdicts.what_is_true: All three are in code and in the public pin: sky_check holds every band's luminance change to 0.05 a second, a town's glow ramps over at least 1 s (look.gd:687), and a hit tints the body 0.6 of the way to white at most 3 times a second per body and 4 in all, beside the register (look.gd:859-866, sim_host.gd:382-399). A 0.05-a-second drift is nowhere near a flash. sky_check runs only in the EP's local render-gates.sh, not CI; whether the sky is in the required flash clips was not checked.
verdicts.fix: Close the open half by listing which flash clips include the dynamic sky; put sky_check in CI once CI runs again.

verdicts.claim: A flashing notice is the first thing in a session: opaque, no timeout, closed only by its own buttons, and worded with Legal's cleared lines (RL-192), which the accessibility audit found identical.
verdicts.what_is_true: At HEAD the gate is as described (ui_notice.gd:3-5; no bypass when the lock is on, ui_hud.gd:1509-1511), and terms.json matches RL-192 word for word. But the live /play/ pack (pin 257a766c) still shows the old in-game words, 'We are fixing them' and 'analyser', which Legal called untrue and not cleared. RL-200 excuses them only until 2026-11-08, and with CI dead nothing will flag it after that date. The cleared words on the HTML gate in front of /play/ soften the harm.
proof: live index.pck photo_body_a ends "We are fixing them."; lock_reduce_flashing true; commit 257a766
tools/site-ui-excuse.json until 2026-11-08, ruling RL-200 kept by RL-207
verdicts.fix: Once CI is repaired, move the pin to a commit with the RL-192 strings or take /play/ down, before the excuse lapses; correct the record to say the cleared words are at HEAD and on the click-through, not yet in the live game.
verdicts.belongs_to: Tools (site pin), with Legal and UI

verdicts.claim: Wind-up, counter, caught and guard-broken marks: a hollow thin shrinking ring with no text, no face marks and no gold, white or red flash.
verdicts.what_is_true: The rule exists as m07 and m08 and is built and tested (shots_view.gd:708, effects_check.gd:3937,4232). Its stated reason is 'no readout or scanner look, no mark 7', which is distance from a well-known franchise, so it is originality. The claim also overstates the rule: m08 bans only a full-screen or body-wide gold, white or red flash, not every such flash. Red is separately refused by the flash register (flash_registry.gd:20). RL-246 and RL-248 cite RL-240, RL-227 and k03 for colour, not RL-078.
proof: docs/legal/movegen-banned.json m08 why: "no readout or scanner look, no mark 7"
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A colour taboo read as flash-safety law makes later look choices (such as RL-248's gold ring) need Legal rulings they would not need on safety grounds.
verdicts.fix: Move to Legal's originality record and quote m08's real scope (full-screen or body-wide only); leave red-flash safety to the register.

verdicts.claim: f01 echo ceiling: the earlier pass rested on VFX's false claim of at most two echoes alive at once. It was fixed in 868c15ee to two echoes; a staggered third is acceptable only if a tick-by-tick strip shows at most two alive.
verdicts.what_is_true: The facts hold: 868c15ee (2026-10-06, VFX) says a perfect timed blow draws two echoes, not three, and ghost_tally.gd counts after-images at every instant. f01's stated reason is 'the many-armed barrage blur', so this is an originality ceiling, not a flash limit. The real lesson is process: Legal ruled on a director's unmeasured claim. Not checked: whether a tick-by-tick strip exists for a staggered third.
proof: 868c15ee subject: a perfect timed blow draws two echoes, not three
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: An originality ghost cap filed under flash safety suggests a photosensitivity limit that does not exist.
verdicts.fix: Move to Legal's originality record; as process, Legal rulings that rest on a director's numbers should cite a measurement or strip.

verdicts.claim: UI launch marks pass as moving marks: the recharging ring at 1 Hz and the tug ring at 3 Hz, listed under fx04 and k06.
verdicts.what_is_true: The pass is sound against the standard: WCAG 2.3.1 allows up to three flashes a second, and a thin ring is far below its area estimate (341 x 256 px at 1024 x 768). But Legal's own margin is broken in the shipped steady form. Under Reduce flashing the tug's beat bar fills for 0.12 s after every 20-tick pulse, a 3 Hz blink where fx04 says 1.5 Hz or slower and k06 says static, and hud_check only tests 'at most 3 a second'. This is latent: beamStruggle is disabled at HEAD and a8bc66e2 and absent from the pin's sim.
proof: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold.html (accessed 2026-11-07): "no more than three general flashes and / or no more than three red flashes"
external: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold.html (accessed 2026-11-07): "using a 341 x 256 pixel rectangle anywhere on the displayed screen area"
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed); the inventory's worry that 3 Hz sits at the flash limit overstates a sub-threshold stroke.
verdicts.fix: Before beamStruggle is switched on, make the steady beat bar hold or change at 1.5 Hz or slower, and add that rate assertion to hud_check.

verdicts.claim: The UI's gold legend ring in the first three struggles never stretches into an edge line, makes at most two changes a second, holds steady under Reduce flashing, reads by shape as well as colour, and its clips still go through the analyser.
verdicts.what_is_true: Every condition is in code. The ring now has its own colour (#c6f24a, not gold, so the record's 'gold' is stale), a 0.1 s ramp, stays lit across beats under 0.5 s apart, holds steady under Reduce flashing, and is a ring with six ticks inside the legend. hud_check asserts all this locally, and no workflow runs it. A ring of about 25 px is far below WCAG's area threshold. Latent: beam struggles are disabled in data. Not checked: whether its clips went through the pixel analyser, which only runs by hand.
verdicts.fix: Correct the record (own colour, not gold); run hud_check in CI once CI works.
